title: Dark Chocolate Orange Tart with Candied Orange
summary: A crisp orange-scented pastry case with a silky baked dark chocolate and orange filling, finished with candied orange slices.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (60-70% cocoa solids), finely chopped
ingredients.note: check the label for soya and milk

ingredients.item: soft unsalted butter, in thin slices
large eggs, beaten, at room temperature

steps.title: Candied orange
steps.text: simmer the sugar and water in the frying pan until dissolved, add the orange slices in one layer and simmer very gently 30-40 min, turning once, until the rind is translucent. Lift onto baking paper to cool. Gentle simmering keeps the slices whole.

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: whisk the yolk with the 2 tbsp cream. Blitz the flour, sugar, salt and 1 tsp zest, add the butter and blitz to crumbs, then pour in the yolk mix and blitz until it gathers into a ball. Wrap and chill 30 min.

steps.title: Line and blind bake
steps.text: roll to a 30 cm round, line the tin and freeze 30 min. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan), line the case with paper and beans and bake on the tray 20 min, then 5-10 min uncovered until golden. Reduce to 150 °C (130 °C fan).

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: heat the 300 ml cream with the 2 tsp zest and salt to a simmer, leave 10 min to infuse, reheat and strain over the chocolate. Cover 5 min, stir smooth from the centre, then mix in the butter and the eggs until glossy.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: pour into the case and bake 20-25 min, until set at the edge with a faint wobble in the middle. It firms as it cools, so take it out with a slight wobble.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: cool at least 2 h, then top with the candied orange slices and a little extra zest.

tips: A common mistake is boiling the cream with the chocolate, which can make it grainy; pour hot cream over instead.
Grate only the orange part of the peel; the white pith is bitter.
Cut with a hot, dry knife for neat slices.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in a cool place for 1 day, or in the fridge for up to 3 days; bring to room temperature before serving.
